editorial.headline: Precious-Metal Goods With a Bali Registration Block
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 32119 covers specialised precious-metal goods, nationally open to foreign ownership but blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the record’s moratorium rule.
editorial.body:
KBLI 32119 is not a broad jewellery category. The record frames it as the manufacture of other valuable goods from precious metals: precious-metal coins, whether or not they are legal tender; engraving services on personal items, including items that are not themselves made of precious metal; and specialised precious-metal articles for technical and laboratory use. Its scope also reaches comparable precious-metal goods for other uses, such as watch straps, watch bands, cuff links, and cigarette cases.

That mix gives the code a particular character. It sits where craft, personalisation, and small high-value metal objects meet more technical applications. The laboratory examples in the record are concrete: spatulas, crucibles, cupels, platinum grills for catalysts, and anodes for electroplating. In plain English, this is a manufacturing activity for precious-metal goods that are valuable, specialised, or functional, without turning the code into a catch-all for every precious-metal product.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, so it can describe anything from a small engraving or precious-metal workshop to a larger manufacturing setup, provided the activity stays within the stated scope. Nationally, the PMA position is also clear: the activity is marked TERBUKA, with pma_max_asing at 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. On the national reading alone, this is therefore foreign-open up to full foreign ownership.

Bali changes the practical answer. The record marks l4_bali_blocked as true and gives the reason as: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026”. The linked moratorium rule is broader still: “Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA (island-wide, permanent)”. For a foreign founder, that is the honest conclusion. Nationally, KBLI 32119 is open. In Bali, the record says PMA registration is blocked today, not because the national foreign-ownership ceiling is low, but because Bali’s recorded moratorium blocks this risk class for PMA registration.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, KBLI 32119 is open; in Bali, the record says PMA registration is blocked today.
